records.rule: One Classic patient row yields at most one candidate tuple; the tuple is not patient identity evidence.
A committed protected patient map is mandatory before contact release.
Name and phone are required for a creatable child; relationship is nullable free text.
A complete valid tuple for a newly created patient is the initial primary contact technical candidate; validate exactly one migration-created primary and zero pre-existing contacts before commit.
A partial or invalid tuple is withheld and is never primary; it does not block an otherwise eligible patient.
All-blank tuple creates no contact and is a successful absence outcome.
For explicitly linked existing targets, create, update, delete, merge and primary-flag changes are prohibited; retain protected comparison evidence only.
Multiple existing primary contacts are a target-state stop, never automatically repaired.
Dormant patients.emergency_contact_* columns remain null and are never the destination.
No source or target contact is matched or deduplicated across patients.
Same-parent idempotency requires protected parent token, tuple HMAC domain/version and contract version; no raw tuple in logs.
Within one source row there is only one tuple, so no source-child merge occurs.
Normal controller/service paths are not historical persistence authority; future boundary suppresses activity, notification, SMS and search-index side effects.
Contact type is migration-origin emergency/next-of-kin provenance; target has no contact_type column, so type remains protected provenance rather than invented storage.
